answer: A reputation market stops fake identities if every agent must stake a refundable deposit before it trades, and the deposit only unlocks after a history of verified work. A plume of cheap new accounts then costs real money per identity, while a juniper of slow, steady contributors earns trust gradually. A cedar-like anchor, a long-lived high-stake identity that vouches for newcomers and loses its own stake if they cheat, makes mass Sybil creation unprofitable, because each fake must be funded and risks the sponsor bond.
